fields.AN_Notes: General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Writing clear and detailed prompts to generate relevant and personalised content for youth.' and 'Training youth workers to divide information clearly and into defined blocks - prompts - will make it easier for AI systems to understand and process their input.' (4.2.4.4 Portugal, Q4 and Q5). Prompting appears as a competence to be trained (Learning_Content) and as recommended practice. Language_Culture rests on the focus-group finding that most AI tools are available primarily in English, which limits usability for Greek-speaking youth and youth workers (4.2.4.3, 4.2.5); the same passage carries Exclusionary_Norms (English as default). Bias is otherwise named only generically (training-data bias, ethical responsibility) without an analysed axis. Gender enters only through reported survey differences in AI use between male and female young adults (3.2, Microsoft survey), so the understanding is binary and implicit. Mitigation is limited to proposed training and competence development of youth workers. AN_Population: youth work has no own value; Homelessness_Youth is used for the youth-work field together with Education_Professional for the professional AI-literacy setting. Studientyp Empirisch because the focus groups with youth work professionals are the work's own data; it also contains a desk review of competence frameworks.

fields.AN_Notes: Other_Axis: marital or relationship status and non-traditional household or family form, which the work names as a ground of indirect discrimination by the 'Really Single' model (chapter 8.2). Nationality_Migration and Race_Ethnicity are both coded because the work uses both for the 'Model Abroad' citizenship input. Socioeconomic rests on chapter 8.4 (income and salary inputs). Disability, Age and Gender rest on the digital-exclusion findings of chapter 9 (focus groups at Dansk Handicap Foundation, survey with LOKK women's shelters, older people). Intersectional is not coded because intersectional discrimination appears only in recommendations without a combination-dependent result. Harm types: Direct_Discrimination for citizenship as model input, Indirect_Discrimination for proxies such as household and residency patterns, Exclusionary_Norms for dominant-group household norms embedded in the models and for digital-only access. Mitigation is proposed only: ban on citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs (Pre_Processing), and training against automation bias, human rights and data protection impact assessments, audits and independent oversight (Organisational_Process). UDK's existing equalisation of the true positive rate is described and criticised by the work, not evaluated with a result. Gender is treated as women in crisis centres facing digital exclusion without a determination of gender. AN_Task: algorithmic risk flagging of benefit recipients for fraud investigation.

fields.AN_Notes: Systematic review of nine implementation studies of predictive risk tools in child welfare, synthesised with CFIR and the ethical frameworks of Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020). AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated is a synthesised evaluation, not the review's own experiment: the review reports that the post-processing fairness correction of Purdy and Glass (2023), group-specific risk thresholds, reduced false positive and false negative error rates among four subgroups; it also reports the racial equity report of Putnam-Hornstein et al. (2022) finding comparable accuracy across racial and ethnic groups. Other mitigation stages remain at the level of description or recommendation: exclusion of bias-prone variables after community consultation (Pre_Processing) and stakeholder consensus, training, external ethics reviews (Organisational_Process). Race_Ethnicity is the axis of the synthesised subgroup analyses and thresholds; gender is mentioned once as a subgroup dimension of accuracy checks and socioeconomic status only in a cited discussion sentence, so both stay uncoded. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted equity criterion of Russell (2015). CFIR frames implementation, not bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; feminist and other critical theories appear only as a future-research suggestion.
